# Exact transverse gain in a two-contact critical pair slab
fibers. It supplies a sharp geometric gain and an all-dimensional scalar
bound, not the unresolved numerical three-plus-two global cap credit.
The one-dimensional moment estimate and its closed-form consequence
were proposed by root; the proof below includes all their details.

## 1. Actual two-contact setting and the pair residual

Let C be a convex body in R x R^d, d>=2. Suppose two globally deepest
points of positive depth occur at integer bases 0 and 1 in positive
d-volume fibers.
Apply the single fiber shear subtracting their affine interpolation, so
the points are (0,0) and (1,0). This fixes the integer coordinate and
preserves fiber volume. If a genuine critical two-cap circuit is based
at (1,0), normalize its opposite continuous normals to u,-u, |u|=1.
The individual nonpositive-margin inequalities at the other deepest
point give its caps the form

    H_+={u.x+b_+(z-1)>=0},
    H_-={-u.x+b_-(z-1)>=0},       b_+,b_->=0.            (1)

The following geometry only requires this normal form and 0 in int C_1.
Positive depth in an actual positive fiber implies that interior
condition, by the boundary lemma in Section 2 of
`candidate 4a38a3cfd6733dce`.

Put

    J={x:-b_-<=u.x<=b_+},
    E=C_1 intersect u-perp.                            (2)

Then E is a full-dimensional (d-1)-body in u-perp and contains zero in
its relative interior. At z<1, the closed residual of the pair is

    R_z=C_z intersect (1-z)J.                          (3)

The union-complement itself uses strict inequalities. Each boundary is
an ambient nonvertical plane and has zero d-volume in every fiber, so
(3) has exactly the correct residual mass. No positive boundary fiber
mass is removed by this replacement.

For t in [0,1) for which the section at z(t)=-t/(1-t) exists, define

    A_t=(1-t)C_(z(t)),       D_t=A_t intersect J.        (4)

Thus R_(z(t))=D_t/(1-t). The parameter is a real projective coordinate
used only to express an inclusion; integer fibers are still measured
at their original bases and with their exact scale factor.

## 2. Strong erosion and transverse section inclusions

**Lemma 1.** If 0<=s<t<1 and C_(z(t)) is nonempty, then

    A_t+(t-s)C_1 subset A_s,                            (5)
    D_t+(t-s)E subset D_s.                              (6)

In particular D_t subset D_s. No assumption that C_(z(t)) contains zero
is needed.

Indeed

    z(s)=[(1-t)/(1-s)]z(t)+[(t-s)/(1-s)]1.

Actual convexity supplies the corresponding Minkowski inclusion of
sections. Multiplying by 1-s gives (5). For a point in D_t and a point
in E, the added term has zero u-coordinate, so their sum still belongs
to J. This gives (6). Since 0 belongs to E, nestedness follows.

For v in u-perp and h real, use the slice notation

    D_t(h)={v:hu+v belongs to D_t}.

Equation (6) gives, at every nonempty slice,

    D_t(h)+(t-s)E subset D_s(h).                        (7)

This is the new dimensional feature of the slab: the source at the
other genuine contact supplies a full (d-1)-dimensional additive body
without consuming any of the residual slab's width.

## 3. Exact planar gain and its integer form

When d=2, let L=H_1(E)>0 and let w_t be the length of the projection of
D_t onto u. Set w_t=0 for an empty set. Length addition for intervals,
followed by Fubini in (7), gives

    |D_s|-|D_t| >= (t-s)L w_t.                          (8)

This holds for lower-dimensional nonempty D_t as well. A slice can be a
singleton, and adding (t-s)E still contributes its full length. A
zero-width projection gives the trivial inequality.

At integer z=-j, j>=1, write V_j=|R_(-j)| and w_j=width_u R_(-j).
Take t=j/(j+1) and s=(j-1)/j. The scales are

    |D_t|=V_j/(j+1)^2,  |D_s|=V_(j-1)/j^2,
    w_t=w_j/(j+1),      t-s=1/[j(j+1)].

Consequently (8) is exactly

    (j+1)^2 V_(j-1)-j^2 V_j >= j L w_j.               (9)

Whenever the remote residual has positive area, its width is positive,
so the normalized residual areas strictly decrease with distance from
the left contact. Formula (9) is not an unweighted monotonicity claim
about the original integer residual volumes V_j.

## 4. A self-contained concave-moment estimate

Let p>=1 be an integer, let h>=0 be a continuous concave function on an
interval of length w>0, positive on its interior, and set

    V=integral h(v)^p dv>0,
    A=((p+1)V/w)^(1/p).                                (10)

Then, for each integer 0<=k<=p,

    integral h(v)^k dv >= w A^k/(k+1),                 (11)

with the k=0 integral interpreted as w.

Here is a direct proof. Let H=max h. The two line segments from a
maximizer to zero at the interval endpoints lie below h, so their
tent has p-moment w H^p/(p+1). Thus A>=H. The normalized tail

    T(a)=length{v:h(v)>a}/w

has T(0)=1 and is concave on [0,H]: superlevel intervals combine by
Minkowski interpolation, whose length is additive. This remains true
if a maximum plateau makes the endpoint value T(H)=0 a downward jump.
Set T=0 above H and compare it with U(a)=(1-a/A)_+.
On [0,H], T-U is concave and vanishes at zero. Its quotient by a>0 is
therefore nonincreasing. On (H,A) the difference is nonpositive. Thus
T-U has at most one change from positive to negative.

Layer cake and (10) give

    integral_0^infinity a^(p-1)[T(a)-U(a)]da=0.          (12)

For 0<k<p, choose a crossing point c. Multiplication by the decreasing
weight a^(k-p), and subtraction of the constant c^(k-p) using (12),
shows that

    integral a^(k-1)[T(a)-U(a)]da>=0.

If no positive crossing exists, (12) forces equality almost everywhere
and the same conclusion holds. Layer cake now gives (11). The cases
k=0 and k=p are immediate. All integrals at zero are finite for k>0;
no singular k=0 layer-cake formula is used.

For a convex body's slice profile the function h may only have downward
endpoint jumps in its displayed closed-section values. Alter those two
values to their one-sided limits. Concavity and all volume integrals
are unchanged, so the same proof applies.

## 5. Closed-form gain in every dimension

Assume D_t has positive d-volume V and u-width w>0. Put

    p=d-1,   e=H_p(E)^(1/p),   a=t-s,
    A=(d V/w)^(1/p).                                  (13)

Brunn--Minkowski in the p-dimensional slices in (7) gives

    |D_s| >= integral (h(v)+a e)^p dv,
    h(v)=H_p(D_t(v))^(1/p),                            (14)

where the integral is over the width interval of D_t. This slice-root
profile is concave by ordinary Brunn--Minkowski. Apply (11) term by term
to the binomial expansion in (14). The resulting finite sum evaluates
exactly to

    |D_s| >= w [(A+a e)^(p+1)-(a e)^(p+1)]/[(p+1)A].  (15)

Indeed the sum is w integral_0^1 (A v+a e)^p dv. At a=0, its value is
w A^p/(p+1)=V. For d=2, (15) is precisely V+a e w, hence agrees with
(8). No constant is hidden in this estimate.

The positive-volume version (15) avoids division by zero. For a
nonempty zero-volume D_t with width w>0, (7) still gives the valid
bound |D_s|>=a^p H_p(E)w by adding E to every nonempty slice. For
zero width, nestedness remains available and no positive d-volume
gain is asserted from transverse addition alone.

## 6. Sharpness with actual critical contacts in every dimension

The gain is sharp even when the two contact points are genuinely
globally deepest and every integer fiber is strictly lighter than half
the total mass.

Take a unit u and a centrally symmetric full p-dimensional body
E_0 subset u-perp. Fix a_0>0 and let

    K=conv(E_0, a_0 u, -a_0 u),
    C=[-1,2] times K.                                 (16)

Then C has exactly four positive integer fibers, all equal to K. Write
W=|K|, so M=4W. The two actual points (0,0),(1,0) have raw depth at
least 3W/2 against EVERY ambient halfspace. For a through-(0,0) cap
with nonzero continuous normal, the contributions of the fibers -1
and 1 add to W by central symmetry, the own fiber contributes W/2,
and the remaining fiber contributes a nonnegative amount. For a cap
through (1,0), pair bases 0 and 2 instead. A pure-integer containing
halfspace has mass at least 2W. Parallel translation to a through-point
cap proves the same lower bound for every containing halfspace.

Now take the pair at base 1

    H_+={u.x+(a_0/2)(z-1)>=0},
    H_-={-u.x+(a_0/2)(z-1)>=0}.                        (17)

The fiber at -1 contributes zero volume to each, including any
supporting boundary trace. The fibers 0 and 2 together contribute W,
and the own fiber contributes W/2. Thus both actual caps have mass
B=3W/2 and are critical at (1,0).

For a genuine rank-two triple at base 0, choose any independent
continuous normals v_1,v_2 and v_3=-v_1-v_2, and put

    c_i=h_K(v_i)/2>0,
    G_i={v_i.x-c_i z>=0},       i=1,2,3.               (18)

Each excludes the fiber at 2 up to volume zero, the pair -1,1 has total
cap volume W, and the own fiber contributes W/2. These three caps also
have mass B and are critical at (0,0). Their margins have weighted sum
-(c_1+c_2+c_3)z, so their union covers every plane with z<=0. The pair
(17) covers every plane with z>=1. The five original caps therefore
cover all actual integer fibers and prove global maximal raw depth
exactly B. Each individual fiber has mass W<M/2. All contact, cap,
convexity, lattice-completeness, and oblique-halfspace premises are real.

For the slab defined by (17), J={|u.x|<=a_0/2} and E=C_1 intersect
u-perp=E_0. At t=1/2 and s=0,

    D_t=K/2,      D_s=K intersect J.                   (19)

The sections of K at coordinate v are (1-|v|/a_0)E_0. On the common
width interval [-a_0/2,a_0/2], the sections in (19) are therefore

    (1/2-|v|/a_0)E_0,
    (1-|v|/a_0)E_0.

Every transverse slice inclusion is equality, and the first slice-root
profile is a tent. All moment inequalities (11) and the final estimate
(15) are equalities. This proves sharpness under the genuine-critical
and strict-no-heavy-fiber conditions, for every d>=2.

For the particularly simple planar rectangle calibration, one can
instead take K=[-2,2] times [-1,1], J={|x|<=1}, E={0} times [-1,1].
The same four-layer central-symmetry argument gives M=32 and B=12.
The pair is {plus-or-minus x+z-1>=0}; a critical triple is
{x-z>=0}, {y-z/2>=0}, {-x-y-3z/2>=0}. Its residual data are
V_1=8, w_1=4, V_0=4, H_1(E)=2, and (9) is exactly 16-8=8.

## 7. The same gain for each original left-cap missed residual

Suppose a critical cap at the left contact has the actual normal form

    G_i={v_i.x-c_i z>=0},       c_i>=0.

The sign again follows from its nonpositive margin at (1,0). In the
projective coordinates (4), its slice is {v_i.y+c_i t>=0}. Define

    U_i(t)=D_t intersect {v_i.y<=-c_i t},
    E_i^-=E intersect {v_i.e<=c_i}.                     (20)

The set U_i(t) is the part of the pair residual missed by that original
cap, up to its null hyperplane boundary. Every E_i^- has positive
(d-1)-volume and contains zero: E contains a relative ball around zero,
and cutting that ball by a linear inequality with nonnegative threshold
retains at least a half-ball (or all of it).

For y in U_i(t) and e in E_i^-, equation (6) puts y+(t-s)e in D_s,
and its cap coordinate satisfies

    v_i.(y+(t-s)e)<=-c_i t+(t-s)c_i=-c_i s.

Hence there is the exact simultaneous family of inclusions

    U_i(t)+(t-s)E_i^- subset U_i(s),   for every i.     (21)

Each missed residual therefore obeys the entire section argument and
bound (15), with its own V, width, and e_i=H_(d-1)(E_i^-)^(1/(d-1)).
In the planar integer notation, let U_(i,j) be the area of
R_(-j) intersect G_i^c and let w_(i,j) be its u-width. The exact bound is

    (j+1)^2 U_(i,j-1)-j^2 U_(i,j)
                       >=j H_1(E_i^-) w_(i,j).         (22)

These quantities retain the identities of the original caps. They are
not independently reassigned minima on different fibers. The total
residual gain and the individual missed-residual gains need not have a
favorable difference, so (21)--(22) alone do not establish a sign for
minimum-cap dispersion.

## 8. What this adds, and what remains separate

The exact 3+2 cap accounting is in
`candidate 398b9c9f084b81b8`.
The new input here is the actual transverse additive body supplied by
the other deepest fiber, and its sharp explicit contribution (8), (9),
and (15) to pair-residual growth, together with the original-cap
missed-residual inclusions (21). It uses more than scalar cap-budget
arrays or the pointwise nonpositive margins at the two contacts.

No inequality comparing this gain with the triple's dispersion deficit
and local overlap surplus is proved here. In the sharpness family the
normalized depth is 3/8, above the OC target, so it is neither a bad
minimizer nor a counterexample. A sign estimate for the remaining
3+2 credit requires a further argument retaining those cap quantities.
